reply.bar_clear: Nobody for the side to move is stuck on the bar right now.
reply.bar_you_must: You have checker(s) on the bar — enter them first.
reply.bearing_off:
Bearing off: remove checkers from your home board once all 15 are there.

Borne off so far — White {{whiteOff}}, Black {{blackOff}}.

{{canNow}}

A die larger than your highest occupied point can still bear that highest checker off.
reply.bearing_off_not_yet: The side to move cannot bear off with the current dice.
reply.bearing_off_now: At least one legal bear-off is available right now.
reply.best_move:
The on-device engine likes {{move}} among {{options}} distinct options.

It’s a solid teaching suggestion — not a world-class bot. Look for making points, hitting blots safely, and reducing your own blots.
reply.best_move_game_over: The game is over — open a new game if you want fresh advice.
reply.best_move_none: With {{dice}}, there is no legal move. Pass the turn when you’re ready.
reply.best_move_opening: First roll to decide who starts — then I’ll suggest moves once dice are in play.
reply.best_move_roll_first: Roll the dice first — then ask again and I’ll suggest a move.
reply.blot_summary: Blots (lone checkers): you {{you}}, opponent {{them}}. Lone checkers can be hit.
reply.blots:
Blots on the board: White {{white}}, Black {{black}}.

A blot is a single checker on a point. Landing on an opponent’s blot hits it to the bar.
reply.can_bear_off: You can bear off with the current dice — look for the bear-off tray.
reply.dice:
Each turn you roll two dice and play both numbers if you can (doubles = four moves of that number).

You may use either die first. If only one number is playable, you must play it — usually the larger when both are possible but not both together.
reply.direction:
White moves 24 → 1 (toward the bottom-right home). Black moves 1 → 24 (toward the top-right home).

Think of a horseshoe path around the board: opponent’s home → outer boards → your home.
reply.explain_game_over: Game over — {{winner}} won by bearing off all 15 checkers first.
reply.explain_moving: {{player}} to play with die values [{{dice}}]. About {{moves}} distinct legal landing(s).
reply.explain_no_move: {{player}} rolled {{dice}} but nothing is legal — the turn must be passed.
reply.explain_opening: Opening roll: each side rolls one die. Higher number goes first and plays both dice as the opening roll. Ties re-roll.
reply.explain_rolling: {{player}} should roll the dice to start this turn.
reply.fallback:
I’m a free on-device coach — I explain the live board and rules, but I don’t browse the web.

Try a suggestion chip, or ask about the race, hitting, bearing off, dice, or “what’s a good move?”
reply.hitting:
Hitting: land on a point that holds exactly one opponent checker (a blot). That checker goes to the bar and must re-enter before its owner moves anything else.

You cannot land on a point with two or more enemy checkers — that’s a made point.
reply.must_enter: You have {{count}} on the bar — you must enter before other moves.
reply.race_extra: Checkers borne off: White {{whiteOff}}, Black {{blackOff}}. Pip count ignores borne-off checkers (they’re done).
reply.race_lead: {{leader}} leads the race by {{diff}} pip(s) ({{leaderPips}} vs {{trailerPips}}). Lower pips = closer to finishing.
reply.race_tied: The race is tied at {{pips}} pips each. Pip count is the total distance left to bear off.
reply.welcome:
Hi — I’m your free coach. I run entirely on your device (no account, no charges).

Ask about this position, tap a suggestion, or request a tip. I use the same rules engine as the computer opponent.

graduation.body: You know the goal, the board, how turns work, hitting, and bearing off. A quick check — then your first real game.
graduation.recap_2: Roll two dice; land on open points
graduation.recap_3: Hit blots → they sit on the bar
graduation.recap_4: Bear off only from your home board
graduation.recap_5: Games start with one die each — higher goes first (ties re-roll)
graduation.title: You’re ready to play

learn.home_cta_ready: You’re ready — play a real game

overshoot.body: Nothing is on the 5-point, but you rolled a 5. Bear off from your highest occupied point (the 3) — a larger die still works.
overshoot.hint: Select point 3, then tap the bear-off tray.
overshoot.praise: That’s the overshoot rule — you’ll use it a lot when bearing off.
overshoot.title: Bigger die, still off

try.body: All your checkers are in home (1–6), so you can bear off. You rolled a 3 — take the checker on the 3-point off the board.
try.hint: Select point 3, then tap the bear-off area on the right edge.
try.praise: Off the board! First to bear off all 15 wins.
try.title: Bear one off

explain.body: Your white checkers move in a horseshoe: from the far side, across, then into your home (points 1–6). Every game starts with the same 2-5-3-5 pattern.
explain.title: The horseshoe path

far.body: Tap the point where your two farthest white checkers start (the 24-point).
far.hint: Look at the top-right — two white checkers on point 24.
far.praise: Those start deep in the opponent’s home and have the longest journey.
far.title: Your farthest checkers

home_stack.body: Tap the big stack of five white checkers already in your home (the 6-point).
home_stack.hint: Bottom-right: five white checkers on point 6.
home_stack.praise: That’s the 2-5-3-5 setup: 2 on 24, 5 on 13, 3 on 8, 5 on 6.
home_stack.title: Your home stack

bar.body: The raised strip in the middle is the bar. Hit checkers wait here. Tap the bar.
bar.hint: Tap the vertical strip between the left and right halves of the board.
bar.praise: Right — hit checkers sit on the bar until they re-enter.
bar.title: The bar

explain.body: You and your opponent each have 15 checkers. Move them around the board and off — first one finished wins.
explain.title: First to bear off wins

home.body: Your home is points 1–6 (bottom-right). Tap any point in your home board.
home.hint: Home is the six points in the bottom-right quadrant — numbered 1 through 6.
home.praise: That’s your home — checkers leave the board from here.
home.title: Find your home board

enter.body: You’re on the bar — you must enter before anything else. Die N enters on point 25−N (a 4 → point 21).
enter.hint: Tap the bar, then point 21 (not 23 — that’s the 2).
enter.praise: You’re back on the board — bar checkers always enter first.
enter.title: Enter from the bar
enter.wrong: That’s the 2 (point 23). Use the 4 — enter on point 21 (25−4).

hit.body: A single checker is a blot. Land on it and it goes to the bar. You rolled a 3 — hit the black blot on the 5-point.
hit.hint: Tap your checker on 8, then tap point 5.
hit.praise: Hit! That black checker is now on the bar.
hit.title: Hit the blot

blocked.body: Two or more opponent checkers block a point — you can’t land there. Tap the blocked black stack on the 5-point.
blocked.hint: The highlighted stack of two black checkers on point 5.
blocked.praise: Right — a made point (2+) is closed. Empty, your own, or a blot (1) are open.
blocked.title: Blocked points

doubles.body: Doubles give you four moves of that number. You rolled 2-2 — that’s four 2s. Move from the 8-point to the 6-point four times.
doubles.hint: Tap the 8-point, then the 6-point. Do this four times — once per die.
doubles.praise: Exactly — doubles mean four moves with that number.
doubles.title: Doubles = four moves

explain.body: Each turn you roll two dice and play both numbers when you can. You may land on empty points, your own checkers, or a lone opponent (a blot).
explain.title: Two numbers, open points

two_dice.body: You rolled 3 and 1. Move the checker on the 8-point three pips (to 5), and the one on the 6-point one pip (to 5).
two_dice.hint: Select a white checker, then tap point 5. Do this for both the 8-point and the 6-point.
two_dice.praise: Nice — both dice used. Same checker or two checkers, both numbers must be played when you can.
two_dice.title: Play both dice

bar.b: Enter that checker before moving anything else
bar.prompt: While you have a checker on the bar, you must…

bear.b: Only after you hit a blot
bear.c: When all 15 checkers are in your home board

blot.a: Any stack of three or more
blot.b: A single checker on a point — it can be hit
